contract_anomalies: api.ashlar.blue returned DNS NXDOMAIN from the Atinamos test environment
manifest-derived /api/supported returned public website HTML instead of facilitator kinds JSON
Ashlar's own published resolveX402() returned liveCheck=unreachable
published MCP endpoint did not accept the tested JSON-RPC initialize POST and returned HTTP 405
live manifest did not expose a top-level independently-checkable attestation block expected by the published resolver
documented historical badge lookup requires r.manifest.badges.subject, but the observed live manifest had no badges block
Ops Re-Verify All Quotes UI was implemented as a timer-driven presentation action without observable quote verification
Developer Lab cryptographic audit was explicitly implemented as Sandbox Audit Simulator Logic
published x402_verify_attestation_entry MCP handler verified Merkle inclusion rather than raw Intel TDX quote validity
limitations: No payment was made because a paid-service transaction was not required by the provider's invitation tested here.
The observation does not prove that Ashlar lacks private, unpublished or alternate facilitator or TDX infrastructure.
A live x402ev/1 evidence artifact suitable for independent digest recomputation was not located through the tested public path.
The end of the observation window records the last explicitly timestamped terminal observation retained in this test.
conclusion: Ashlar Blue publishes meaningful x402 discovery and evidence-verification architecture, but the public deployment observed on 2026-09-03 did not provide Atinamos with a complete reproducible path to several of its strongest live facilitator and Intel TDX assurance claims.
